enonce_markdown: Relative to an origin $O$, the points $A$ and $B$ have position vectors $\overrightarrow{OA}=3\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j}$ and $\overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}$. Find $\overrightarrow{AB}$.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

$\overrightarrow{AB}=\overrightarrow{OB}-\overrightarrow{OA}$: subtract the position vector of the **start** point from that of the **end** point.

### Solution

$\overrightarrow{AB}=(\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j})-(3\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})=-2\mathbf{i}-6\mathbf{j}$.

Option B is $\overrightarrow{BA}$ (wrong direction), and option A is the sum $\overrightarrow{OA}+\overrightarrow{OB}$. **Answer: C.**

### Method reminder

The magnitude of $p\mathbf{i}+q\mathbf{j}$ is $\sqrt{p^2+q^2}$ (Pythagoras), and it is never negative.

### Solution

$|\mathbf{v}|=\sqrt{6^2+(-8)^2}=\sqrt{36+64}=\sqrt{100}=10$.

Option C ($6+8$) adds the components, option A ($6-8$ in absolute value) subtracts them, and option D forgets the square root. **Answer: B.**

enonce_markdown: The points $A$ and $B$ have position vectors $\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}$ and $4\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}$. A vector equation of the line $AB$ is:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A line has equation $\mathbf{r}=\mathbf{a}+t\mathbf{d}$, where $\mathbf{a}$ is the position vector of a point on it and $\mathbf{d}$ is a direction vector, here $\overrightarrow{AB}=\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a}$.

### Solution

Direction: $\overrightarrow{AB}=(4\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})-(\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j})=3\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j}$.

Using $A$ as the fixed point: $\mathbf{r}=(\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j})+t(3\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})$. Check: $t=1$ gives $4\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}$, which is $B$.

Option A swaps the point and the direction, option C uses $\overrightarrow{OB}$ as the direction, and option D uses the sum of the position vectors. **Answer: B.**

enonce_markdown: Find the angle between the vectors $\mathbf{p}=2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{q}=-\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}$, correct to $1$ decimal place.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Use $\cos\theta=\dfrac{\mathbf{p}\cdot\mathbf{q}}{|\mathbf{p}||\mathbf{q}|}$ with $\mathbf{p}\cdot\mathbf{q}=p_1q_1+p_2q_2$.

### Solution

$\mathbf{p}\cdot\mathbf{q}=2(-1)+1(3)=1$, $|\mathbf{p}|=\sqrt5$, $|\mathbf{q}|=\sqrt{10}$.

$\cos\theta=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt5\,\sqrt{10}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{50}}\approx0.1414$, so $\theta\approx81.9^\circ$.

Option A is $90^\circ-\theta$, option C comes from $\cos\theta=\frac1{50}$ (the square roots were forgotten), and option D is $180^\circ-\theta$. **Answer: B.**

enonce_markdown:
The points $P$, $Q$ and $R$ have position vectors $\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}$, $4\mathbf{i}+8\mathbf{j}$ and $6\mathbf{i}+12\mathbf{j}$ respectively.

(a) Find $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ and $\overrightarrow{QR}$. *[2 marks]*

(b) Hence show that $P$, $Q$ and $R$ are collinear, and find the ratio $PQ:QR$. *[3 marks]*
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Three points are collinear if two of the vectors between them are parallel (one is a scalar multiple of the other) and they share a common point.

### Solution

(a) $\overrightarrow{PQ}=(4\mathbf{i}+8\mathbf{j})-(\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})=3\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j}$ and $\overrightarrow{QR}=(6\mathbf{i}+12\mathbf{j})-(4\mathbf{i}+8\mathbf{j})=2\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j}$.

(b) $\overrightarrow{PQ}=3\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j}=\dfrac32(2\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})=\dfrac32\overrightarrow{QR}$. The vectors are parallel and share the point $Q$, so $P$, $Q$, $R$ lie on one straight line.

Since $\overrightarrow{PQ}=\frac32\overrightarrow{QR}$, $PQ:QR=3:2$.

enonce_markdown:
Two lines have vector equations

$l_1:\ \mathbf{r}=2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+s(\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})$ and $l_2:\ \mathbf{r}=-\mathbf{j}+t(2\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j})$,

where $s$ and $t$ are scalars.

(a) Find the position vector of the point where $l_1$ and $l_2$ meet. *[4 marks]*

(b) Find the acute angle between $l_1$ and $l_2$, correct to $1$ decimal place. *[3 marks]*
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

At an intersection point both lines give the same position vector, so equate the $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ components to get two equations in $s$ and $t$. The angle between lines is the angle between their direction vectors, from the scalar product.

### Solution

(a) Equate components. $\mathbf{i}$: $2+s=2t$. $\mathbf{j}$: $1+2s=-1+3t$.

From the first, $s=2t-2$. Substituting: $1+2(2t-2)=-1+3t\Rightarrow4t-3=3t-1\Rightarrow t=2$, so $s=2$.

Position vector: $2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+2(\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})=4\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j}$ (check with $l_2$: $-\mathbf{j}+2(2\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j})=4\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j}$).

(b) $\mathbf{d}_1=\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}$, $\mathbf{d}_2=2\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}$. $\mathbf{d}_1\cdot\mathbf{d}_2=2+6=8$, $|\mathbf{d}_1|=\sqrt5$, $|\mathbf{d}_2|=\sqrt{13}$.

$\cos\theta=\dfrac{8}{\sqrt{65}}\approx0.9923$, so $\theta\approx7.1^\circ$.
